answers.q1: Maven, through the committed Maven Wrapper (./mvnw, Maven 3.9.16, Java 17). build.gradle also exists, but README and CI use Maven. Install dependencies with: ./mvnw -B dependency:go-offline (Maven also resolves them on the first build).
answers.q4: CI has no separate lint job. Its only build command is ./mvnw -B verify (.github/workflows/maven-build.yml), and the checks run inside it because spring-javaformat:validate and the nohttp checkstyle check are bound to the validate phase. To run just those checks: ./mvnw -B validate
answers.q5: src/main/resources/static/resources/css/petclinic.css is generated from src/main/scss/*.scss by the libsass plugin in the css profile (regenerate with ./mvnw generate-resources -P css, and edit the .scss files instead). src/main/resources/static/resources/fonts/* are vendored third-party webfonts (Montserrat, Varela Round). target/ is build output (gitignored). Bootstrap is fetched as a webjar at build time, not vendored in the repo.

q1.reason: Uses Maven wrapper ./mvnw with a dependency resolution command (dependency:go-offline), matching the accepted Maven wrapper answer.

q2.reason: ./mvnw -B test matches the accepted ./mvnw test (with the CI -B flag).

q4.reason: Identifies ./mvnw -B verify as CI's command and gives ./mvnw -B validate to run the bound spring-javaformat and nohttp checks, matching accepted answers.

q5.reason: Correctly names petclinic.css as generated from scss (regenerate command via generate-resources -P css is functionally consistent with the css profile) and also notes target/; extra vendored fonts detail is harmless.
